en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll start telling stories about the past with one small ending: -ed. Let's take it step by step.

steps.title: One ending for the past: -ed
steps.text: You know was and were. Now let's talk about actions in the past: I walked, I cooked, I worked.
steps.body:
In Indonesian the **verb** (the doing word) never changes: *Kemarin saya jalan kaki ke kantor*. Only *kemarin* shows it's the past. English changes the verb itself: add **-ed**. **Yesterday I walked to the office.** This is the **past simple**: an action that finished at a time in the past.
- It's the **same for everyone**: *I walked, she walked, they walked* (no -s).
- **No was before it**: 'I was cook dinner' ✗ → **I cooked dinner**. *was/were* is only the past of am/is/are.

steps.title: Spelling the -ed
steps.text: Most verbs just take -ed, but a few endings change the spelling.
steps.body:
(**Vowels** = a, e, i, o, u; **consonants** = all other letters.)
- Ends in **e** → just **+ d**: *lived, danced*.
- **Consonant + y** → **y → ied**: *try → tried*. But **vowel + y** just takes -ed: *played, stayed*.
- **Short verb of one beat** ending in **one vowel + one consonant** → **double** the last letter: *stop → stopped*. Why? 'stoped' would look like *hoped* ('houpt').
- Longer verbs said strong at the front just add -ed: *VI-sit → visited*, *O-pen → opened*. And w, x, y are never doubled: *fixed*.

British *travelled*, American *traveled*: both are correct.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas has an English test today. Think about yesterday.

question.prompt: Complete: Yesterday Dimas ___ for his English test.
question.explanation: **study** ends in a consonant (d) + y, so **y → ied**: **studied**. 'studyed' keeps the y, and 'was study' is wrong: was is only the past of am/is, not a sign for every verb.

steps.title: How -ed sounds
steps.text: -ed is always written the same, but it has three sounds. It's like the -s ending (works, plays, watches).
steps.body:
Listen to the **last sound** of the verb:
- **'t'** after sounds with **no buzz** in your throat (p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x): *worked* = 'workt', *liked* = 'laikt'.
- **'d'** after vowel sounds and sounds **with a buzz** (b, g, l, m, n, r, v, z): *played* = 'pleid', *lived* = 'livd'.
- **'id'**, one extra **beat** (syllable, *suku kata*), **only after t or d**: *wanted* = 'WON-tid', *needed* = 'NII-did'.

Don't add a beat everywhere ('work-ed' ✗), and don't drop the ending: *I walk* and *I walked* must sound different.

steps.title: Listen to the ending
steps.text: Say each verb out loud before you choose.

question.prompt: In which past verb is -ed an extra beat, 'id'?
question.explanation: **wait** ends in a **t** sound, so -ed is said 'id' and adds a beat: **WEI-tid**. *cooked* is one beat ('kukt'), and *cleaned* is one beat too ('kliind').

steps.title: Finished, before now
steps.text: These time words tell you the action is finished: use verb + -ed.

timeline.title: Before now and now
timeline.caption: last year, last month, a week ago, yesterday → verb + -ed. ago counts back from now: a week ago = seven days back from today.

steps.title: last or ago?
steps.text: Indonesian says *lalu* for both. English has two words.
steps.body:
- **No number** → **last**: *minggu lalu* = **last week**, *hari Minggu lalu* = **last Sunday**. No *the* and no *on* before it.
- **A number** (or *a / an*) → **ago**, after the length of time: *dua hari yang lalu* = **two days ago**, *sejam yang lalu* = **an hour ago**.

Not 'two years before': *before* needs something after it (*before lunch*). And *tadi malam / kemarin malam* = **last night**, *tadi pagi* = **this morning**. The time word can go at the end or at the start of the sentence.

steps.title: In real sentences
steps.text: Here are -ed verbs and time words together.
steps.body: Look at the time words: **last weekend** (no number), **a week ago** / **an hour ago** (a length of time + ago), **yesterday afternoon**.

examples.en: Rina stayed at home last weekend.
examples.id: Rina di rumah saja akhir pekan lalu.

examples.en: My father painted the fence yesterday afternoon.
We booked the train tickets a week ago.
examples.id: Kami memesan tiket kereta seminggu yang lalu.

examples.en: Bu Ani opened her warung an hour ago.
examples.id: Bu Ani membuka warungnya sejam yang lalu.

steps.title: Count back
steps.text: Today is Friday. Count back from now.

options: Budi visited the dentist three days ago.
Budi visited the dentist three days before.
Budi visited the dentist ago three days.
question.prompt: Today is Friday. Budi visited the dentist on Tuesday. Which sentence is right?
question.explanation: From Tuesday to Friday is **three days**, counted back from now, so: **three days ago**. **ago** comes after the length of time, and *before* isn't used to count back from now.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina tells you about her weekend.

options: Rina cooked rendang on last Sunday.
question.prompt: Which sentence means 'Rina memasak rendang hari Minggu lalu'?
question.explanation: No number, so *lalu* = **last**: **last Sunday**, with no *on* before it (you say *on Sunday*, but just *last Sunday*). **ago** needs a length of time: *three days ago*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Past simple (regular)
artifact.intro: Finished actions in the past: verb + -ed, the same for everyone.
rows: strong at the front: just + ed
tips: Say -ed as **'t'** after p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x (worked = 'workt'), **'d'** after vowels and buzzing sounds (played = 'pleid'), and **'id'**, an extra beat, only after t or d (wanted = 'WON-tid').
**last** + night / week / month / Sunday, with no *the* and no *on*. A length of time + **ago**: *two days ago*, not 'two days before'.
Same form for everyone, and no *was*: **I walked, she walked**, not 'she was walk'.

examples.id: Saya kerja sampai larut tadi malam.

examples.en: My parents travelled to Lombok last year.
examples.id: Orang tuaku pergi ke Lombok tahun lalu.

examples.en: The shop opened an hour ago.

steps.text: Want more? This page has extra exercises, and the video practises the three -ed sounds.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu mulai bercerita tentang masa lalu dengan satu akhiran kecil: -ed. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Satu akhiran untuk masa lalu: -ed
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu was dan were. Sekarang kita ceritakan apa yang kamu **lakukan**: I walked, I cooked, I worked.
steps.body:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **kata kerja** (kata yang menunjukkan kegiatan) tidak pernah berubah: *Kemarin saya jalan kaki ke kantor*. Hanya *kemarin* yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Bahasa Inggris mengubah kata kerjanya sendiri: tambahkan **-ed**. **Yesterday I walked to the office.** Ini namanya **past simple**: kegiatan yang sudah selesai pada suatu waktu di masa lalu.
- Bentuknya **sama untuk semua orang**: *I walked, she walked, they walked* (tanpa -s).
- **Tanpa was di depannya**: 'I was cook dinner' ✗ → **I cooked dinner**. *was/were* hanya bentuk lampau dari am/is/are.

steps.title: Ejaan -ed
steps.text: Kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah -ed, tapi beberapa akhiran mengubah ejaannya.
steps.body:
(**Vokal** = a, e, i, o, u; **konsonan** = semua huruf lainnya.)
- Berakhiran **e** → cukup **+ d**: *lived, danced*.
- **Konsonan + y** → **y → ied**: *try → tried*. Tapi **vokal + y** cukup + ed: *played, stayed*.
- **Kata kerja pendek satu ketukan** yang berakhiran **satu vokal + satu konsonan** → huruf terakhirnya **digandakan**: *stop → stopped*. Kenapa? 'stoped' akan terlihat seperti *hoped* ('houpt').
- Kata kerja yang lebih panjang dan diucapkan kuat di depan cukup + ed: *VI-sit → visited*, *O-pen → opened*. Dan w, x, y tidak pernah digandakan: *fixed*.

Inggris (British) *travelled*, Amerika *traveled*: keduanya benar.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hari ini Dimas ujian bahasa Inggris. Bagaimana dengan kemarin?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Yesterday Dimas ___ for his English test.
question.explanation: **study** berakhiran konsonan (d) + y, jadi **y → ied**: **studied**. 'studyed' masih memakai y, dan 'was study' salah: was hanya bentuk lampau dari am/is, bukan tanda masa lalu untuk semua kata kerja.

steps.title: Bunyi -ed
steps.text: -ed selalu ditulis sama, tapi punya tiga bunyi. Mirip akhiran -s (works, plays, watches).
steps.body:
Dengarkan **bunyi terakhir** kata kerjanya:
- **'t'** setelah bunyi yang **tidak bergetar** di tenggorokan (p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x): *worked* = 'workt', *liked* = 'laikt'.
- **'d'** setelah bunyi vokal dan bunyi yang **bergetar** (b, g, l, m, n, r, v, z): *played* = 'pleid', *lived* = 'livd'.
- **'id'**, tambah satu **ketukan** (suku kata), **hanya setelah t atau d**: *wanted* = 'WON-tid', *needed* = 'NII-did'.

Jangan menambah ketukan di semua kata ('work-ed' ✗), dan jangan hilangkan akhirannya: *I walk* dan *I walked* harus terdengar berbeda.

steps.title: Dengarkan akhirannya
steps.text: Ucapkan setiap kata kerja dengan suara keras sebelum memilih.

question.prompt: Kata kerja lampau mana yang -ed-nya menambah satu ketukan, 'id'?
question.explanation: **wait** berakhiran bunyi **t**, jadi -ed dibaca 'id' dan menambah satu ketukan: **WEI-tid**. *cooked* satu ketukan ('kukt'), dan *cleaned* juga satu ketukan ('kliind').

steps.title: Sudah selesai, sebelum sekarang
steps.text: Kata-kata waktu ini memberi tanda bahwa kegiatannya sudah selesai: pakai kata kerja + -ed.

timeline.title: Sebelum sekarang dan sekarang
timeline.caption: last year, last month, a week ago, yesterday → kata kerja + -ed. ago dihitung mundur dari sekarang: a week ago = tujuh hari sebelum hari ini.

steps.title: last atau ago?
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai *lalu* untuk keduanya. Bahasa Inggris punya dua kata.
steps.body:
- **Tanpa angka** → **last**: *minggu lalu* = **last week**, *hari Minggu lalu* = **last Sunday**. Tanpa *the* dan tanpa *on* di depannya.
- **Dengan angka** (atau *a / an*) → **ago**, sesudah lamanya waktu: *dua hari yang lalu* = **two days ago**, *sejam yang lalu* = **an hour ago**.

Bukan 'two years before': *before* butuh sesuatu sesudahnya (*before lunch* = sebelum makan siang). Lalu *tadi malam / kemarin malam* = **last night**, *tadi pagi* = **this morning**. Kata waktunya bisa di akhir atau di awal kalimat.

steps.title: Dalam kalimat sehari-hari
steps.text: Ini kata kerja -ed dan kata waktu bersama-sama.
steps.body: Perhatikan kata waktunya: **last weekend** (tanpa angka), **a week ago** / **an hour ago** (lamanya waktu + ago), **yesterday afternoon**.

examples.en: Rina stayed at home last weekend.
examples.id: Rina di rumah saja akhir pekan lalu.

examples.en: My father painted the fence yesterday afternoon.
We booked the train tickets a week ago.
examples.id: Kami memesan tiket kereta seminggu yang lalu.

examples.en: Bu Ani opened her warung an hour ago.
examples.id: Bu Ani membuka warungnya sejam yang lalu.

steps.title: Hitung mundur
steps.text: Hari ini hari Jumat. Hitung mundur dari sekarang.

options: Budi visited the dentist three days ago.
Budi visited the dentist three days before.
Budi visited the dentist ago three days.
question.prompt: Hari ini hari Jumat. Budi ke dokter gigi hari Selasa. Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.explanation: Dari Selasa ke Jumat itu **tiga hari**, dihitung mundur dari sekarang, jadi: **three days ago**. **ago** ada sesudah lamanya waktu, dan *before* tidak dipakai untuk menghitung mundur dari sekarang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang akhir pekannya.

options: Rina cooked rendang on last Sunday.
question.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Rina memasak rendang hari Minggu lalu'?
question.explanation: Tidak ada angka, jadi *lalu* = **last**: **last Sunday**, tanpa *on* di depannya (kamu bilang *on Sunday*, tapi cukup *last Sunday*). **ago** butuh lamanya waktu: *three days ago*.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Past simple (beraturan)
artifact.intro: Kegiatan yang sudah selesai di masa lalu: kata kerja + -ed, sama untuk semua orang.
tips: Ucapkan -ed sebagai **'t'** setelah p, k, f, s, sh, ch, x (worked = 'workt'), **'d'** setelah vokal dan bunyi yang bergetar (played = 'pleid'), dan **'id'**, tambah satu ketukan, hanya setelah t atau d (wanted = 'WON-tid').
**last** + night / week / month / Sunday, tanpa *the* dan tanpa *on*. Lamanya waktu + **ago**: *two days ago*, bukan 'two days before'.
Bentuknya sama untuk semua orang, dan tanpa *was*: **I walked, she walked**, bukan 'she was walk'.
